analysis:
The PR adds `--disk` work-disk support to `darkbloom sandbox setup` (SandboxSetupCommand.swift: validate lines 54-70, options 72-76, checkWorkDisks 297-316, ownershipToTurnOn/turnOnOwnership 320-335, chooseWorkDisk 341-368). It also adds `disks` parsing to SandboxSizingPlan and `SandboxTerminal.choose` in SandboxSetupProgress.swift. I found no concrete regression in the supplied source.

TB-013/T-061: the installer is still downloaded over https, staged owner-only, and run through `/bin/sh` with an argv array. No shell string interpolation of disk paths is visible. `--disk` values pass through `SandboxWorkDisk.absolutePath` and are appended by `SandboxInstaller.arguments`/`planArguments`. Neither is in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify option-injection resistance (for example a path beginning with `-`), `~` handling, or quoting. The new `SandboxInstaller.supportsDisks(script)` check is a substring-style capability probe on the downloaded script. It adds no trust, and a tampered installer remains the T-061 residual.

Privilege step: the optional `sudo diskutil enableOwnership <mount>` runs only on an interactive prompt, never with `--yes` (ownershipToTurnOn requires `!confirmed && interactiveInput`), and only after an explicit confirm. The mount comes from `SandboxWorkDisk.volume(at:)` or the candidates list. Whether the child process is argv-based, whether the mount point is validated, and what hostile volume labels do (for example control characters) are in SandboxWorkDisk, which was not supplied.

Plan parsing: the new `disks` array in the installer's plan event is parsed with defaults and `compactMap`. It is not used for any decision in the supplied code, so it has no security effect here. Installer output remains untrusted text rendered to the terminal, as before.

Threat-model gap: TB-013/A-019 should record that VM images and jobs may now live on an operator-chosen external volume. That volume has the same peripheral-controller and UUID-cloning caveats as T-041's cache storage. The CLI only checks APFS and ownership, which is a weaker check than CacheVolume.inspect. The next pass should examine SandboxWorkDisk, SandboxInstaller.arguments/supportsDisks, and the add-on's handling of the volume.
